headline: Wheeler, Schwarber power Phillies past Braves, 4-2
recap: The Phillies beat the Braves 4-2 at Citizens Bank Park on Saturday night. Philadelphia scored twice in the first: Luis Arraez's RBI single drove in Kyle Schwarber, and later in the inning a walk to J.T. Realmuto scored Trea Turner. Philadelphia added a run in the second when Derek Hill scored on a groundout by Schwarber, making it 3-0 before Ronald Acuña Jr.'s solo home run in the third cut it to 3-1. Schwarber answered in the fourth with his 41st home run of the season for a 4-1 lead, and Austin Riley's solo shot in the seventh brought Atlanta within 4-2, where it stayed. Zack Wheeler earned the win, allowing one run over six innings with nine strikeouts; Jonathan Bowlan surrendered Riley's homer in relief, and Jhoan Duran worked a scoreless ninth for the save. Martín Pérez took the loss for Atlanta, charged with four runs over 3.2 innings.
The win keeps the Phillies at 80-62, second in the NL East, four games behind the division-leading Braves, and has Philadelphia on a one-game winning streak.

Philadelphia and Atlanta play the fourth game of their series Sunday at Citizens Bank Park, with Aaron Nola starting for the Phillies opposite the Braves' Tyler Mahle. First pitch is scheduled for 1:10 PM ET. DraftKings has the moneyline even at -110 on both sides, with Philadelphia at +1.5 on the run line (-185).
